content.text: An order whose total including tax and delivery is exactly $25,000 is placed directly without approval.

expected_answer.baseline: order review with total including tax and delivery of $25,000

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied money because the boundary determines whether a $25,000 purchase is blocked for approval or placed directly; auth because the rule governs whether managerial approval is required; user-reach because any Buyer can hit the threshold; change-frequency because price, tax, or delivery calculations can easily introduce threshold regressions.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 is explicitly an over-limit order at $25,001 including tax and delivery, matching the invariant's threshold condition.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 reaches order review in the over-limit state that the banner promise describes.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 reaches the review step where the primary action must change from direct placement to approval submission.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 includes the act of submitting for approval, which is when the request ID is created.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 covers the created approval request after submission, so the pending status promise applies.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 submits as a Buyer and therefore exercises the requester's-name field on the created approval request.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 creates an approval request from a concrete over-limit order total, so the total field promise applies.
[applicability] Applicable because sc-3 submits the approval request, so the submitted-time field promise applies.
[applicability] Not applicable because ac-17 governs orders whose total exceeds $25,000, while sc-4 fixes the total at exactly $25,000.
[applicability] Not applicable because the over-limit banner is promised only for an over-limit order review state, which sc-4 does not enter.
[applicability] Not applicable because the "Submit for Approval" action label applies only to over-limit review, while sc-4 remains on the direct-placement path.
[applicability] Not applicable because sc-4 does not submit for approval and therefore should not create an approval request ID.
[applicability] Not applicable because sc-4 should not create an approval request, so no pending-approval request status exists on this path.
[applicability] Not applicable because the requester-name field is part of the approval-request record created only on approval submission, which sc-4 does not perform.
[applicability] Not applicable because the order-total field named in ac-23 is recorded on an approval request, and sc-4 stays out of that workflow.
[applicability] Not applicable because submitted time is part of the approval-request artifact that sc-4 should never create.
